title: Code distance is at most the block length
statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a natural number $n$, and let $V = \bbf_p^{\,n} \times \bbf_p^{\,n}$ carry the symplectic form $\omega\bigl((x,z),(x',z')\bigr) = \sum_{i} (x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$. For every $\bbf_p$-subspace $S \le V$, the associated code distance $d(S)$ — the least weight $\mathrm{wt}(v) = |\mathrm{supp}(v)|$ attained by a vector $v$ lying in the symplectic orthogonal complement $S^{\perp_\omega}$ but not in $S$ — satisfies $d(S) \le n$.
